heard: A structure 100 times wider than the Milky Way is technically average. In 2022, astronomers used the LOFAR radio network to discover Alceonius, a record-shattering giant. Over 3 billion light years away, this radio galaxy spans at least 16 million light years. That is equivalent to laying over 100 Milky Way's end to end. If our eyes saw radio waves, these lobes would look as large as the Moon. Twin plasma jets launched from the core near light speed to inflate this gargantuan structure. Researchers expected a monster black hole, but found an average host with no star birth. It grew this massive because it sits in a lonely, empty pocket of the cosmic web. This cosmic Titan exists only because it was blown by an ordinary galaxy.
